minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 24, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on April 24, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 20, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

 CS1.  Conference with Legal Counsel-Existing Litigation: Paragraph (1) of subdivision
  (d) of Section 54956.9; Name of case: Webster et al vs. City of Mission Viejo.

 CS2.  Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

City Council Minutes  1  April 24, 2018
  CS3.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation: Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) or (3) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9
  – Threat of Litigation From City of Santa Ana to Compel Homeless
  Management, Support or Housing.

 CS4.  Conference with legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 case).

 CS5.  Conference with legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 case); and
  threat to Public Services or Facilities; Consultation with Bickmore.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:12 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were five Closed Session matters and, in all cases,
the Council received updates and provided direction to staff but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  Recognize the Spring AYSO Region 84, Boys U10 Bruins and the Girls U12
  Dynamite for their Championship Seasons

  Mayor Sachs presented the certificates of recognition.

 P2.  Southern California Edison Reliability Presentation

  The City Council received the presentation.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Lydie Gutfeld, M.V.: Announced that the Marguerite Tennis Center Pavilion won the Public
Facility of the Year Award by the Professional Tennis Registry (PTR).

Grant Lopez, Aliso Viejo: Asked for Council support for candidate Lenore Albert who is running
for Orange County District Attorney.

Ryan Farsai, M.V.: stated that the City placed an illegal LCD sign on his property behind Anthony’s
ARCO on Marguerite and La Paz.
City Council Minutes  2  April 24, 2018
 Madison Breshears, M.V.: expressed concern with lack of security measure at Newhart Middle
School.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of April 10, 2018, as
  presented.

 2.  Check Register Dated March 30, 2018 in the Amount of $807,759.15

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 3.  Check Register Dated April 6, 2018 in the Amount of $1,318,531.25

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2018

  Received and filed.

 5.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2018

  Received and filed.

 6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  February 2018

  Received and filed.

 7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for
  February 2018

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  April 24, 2018
  8.  Fiscal Year 2018-19 SB 1 Road Repair and Accountability Act Project List

  Adopted Resolution 18-16 Adopting a List of Projects for Fiscal Year 2018-19
  Funded by SB 1: The Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017.

 9.  Request by Commissioner Julia Malisos to Complete her term in the Ordinary
  Sequence of Appointments

  Approved request to complete term on Planning and Transportation Commission.

 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

 10.  Economic Development Committee Report

  Received report from SWA Group and Council Member Goodell.

 11.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  No report.

 12.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received report from Council Member Bucknum

 13.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Council Member Kelley

 14.  Veteran's Advisory Committee Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Raths.

 STAFF REPORTS

 15.  Insurance Pool Membership for City General Liability and Worker's
  Compensation Insurance Coverage

  Administrative Services Manager Andrea Pham presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  eliminate Public Agency Risk Sharing Authority of California (PARSAC) from
  consideration and gave staff approval to notify PARSAC of the decision.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  4  April 24, 2018
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

16.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum shared that she attended an annual event with the Cal State Fullerton
Political Science Department where topics are discussed with the students and feedback is given
by local officials. She Congratulated Cal State Fullerton on organizing an enlightening event.
Council Member Bucknum thanked the Marine Adoption Committee and all the volunteers for the
amazing Marine Lake Day at Lake Mission Viejo. She also thanked Lake Mission Viejo
Association Board Members for opening up the lake at no cost. Council member Bucknum
apologized for missing the last City Council Meeting due to a busy work schedule, and announced
she will be missing the May 8 Council Meeting as well.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that the Olympic Promotion Committee will be meeting
tomorrow to discuss bringing in other countries to train in Mission Viejo prior to the Olympic
Games. One of the committee members has met with potential investors who are involved in
creating dormitory facilities. Council Member Goodell announced that the committee will be
expanding to include Community Services Director Mark Nix along with a representative from
Saddleback College.

Council Member Kelley

 17.  Oppose AB2796

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Sachs, to send a letter to
  the State Assembly to express Mission Viejo’s opposition to AB2796, which would
  have the 241 Toll Road end at Oso Parkway in Mission Viejo.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Council Member Kelley announced that she attended the drug trends meeting hosted by County
Supervisor Lisa Bartlett and the Orange County Sheriff’s Department in Laguna Hills. She
indicated that it was very informative and that the opioid drug trend is very alarming. She also
attended the Marine Lake Day, and gave a shout out to volunteer Carol Weidler and praised the
Mission Viejo Lake Association for their generosity in hosting this event. She said she attended
City Council Minutes  5  April 24, 2018
 the Town Hall Meeting held at City Hall on April 18 hosted by Chief Vuong. Topics at the meeting
included crime statistics, the homeless issue, and sober living homes. Council Member Kelley
commended Chief Vuong for a great job. She encouraged everyone to attend the Arts Alive &
Street Painting Festival on April 28 and 29 at the Norman P. Murray Center and announced that
on Saturday April 28, the Sheriff’s Department will be participating in the National Prescription
Medication Take Back Day from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at City Hall and she encouraged residents
to come by and turn in outdated prescription drugs.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked Grant Lopez in the audience for attending the meeting on behalf of
his candidate for Orange County District Attorney, Lenore Albert. He thanked Mark Nix and
employees at the Norman P. Murray Center for helping with the Mission Viejo Rotary’s fund raiser
last week. It was a very successful event raising roughly $14,000 with $5,000 going toward local
charities, and the other $9,000 going to the Rotary Club Foundation which provides local
scholarships and other monies to help the community. Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he
had a wonderful time at the Marine Day at the Lake, and he thanked volunteer Carol Weidler. He
also announced that the Mission Viejo Chamber had their mixer at the Murray Center and the next
mixer is going to be at the Aquatics Center on May 17. He commented that the Chamber is moving
forward with a lot of new members and getting ready for their Restaurant Week and Buy Local
Campaign. Mayor Pro Tem Raths also announced that he enjoyed playing golf with the South
County Economic Coalition at the Aliso Viejo Country Club.

Mayor Sachs

 18.  Report on South Orange County Association of Mayors (SOCAM) Meeting
  Regarding Homeless Housing

  Received oral report.

Mayor Sachs announced that the Town Hall Meeting was very well attended, and included
information on Neighborhood Watch and Business Watch. He said one of the best statistics he
took away was the “observe calls for service” and more police presence which went up three-fold
from last year. Mayor Sachs commented on the increase in use of opioids that are cut with Fentanyl
and the dangers of this use. He spoke about concerns with the homeless camps in the Wilderness
Glen area and said the city’s Quality of Life Officer is doing her best to get some of these people
the services that they need. Mayor Sachs announced that this Thursday he will be attending the
pinning service for the new Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Chief, Brian Fennessy.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:35 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, May 8, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

_____________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk  Approved at the meeting of May 8, 2018

City Council Minutes  6  April 24, 2018
